punchline: The plan stayed the same. Only the starting position changed, and participation went from 37.4 to 85.9 percent.
thirty_sec: In 1998 a large US company changed its retirement plan so that new hires were enrolled automatically, with 3 percent of pay going into a money market fund, unless they opted out. Researchers Madrian and Shea found that 37.4 percent of the earlier group, who had to sign up themselves, took part, against 85.9 percent of those hired under the new rule. Many stayed at the 3 percent default and in the same fund.
